messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: simsem and semTools support the blavaan object?
parts:
Right now I don't think there's a function in semTools to support blavaan objects. I'm sure some are coming but not yet. 

For simsem, blavaan support is on the list for the next versions (no promises when we'll have it built in). If you want to use blavaan with simsem you can with the current version. The model object in the sim function will accept a function that fits a model and returns a list (see the help documentation for the sim function in simsem for more details). Using this capability you could write a function running a model with blavaan and returning the correct valeus.

Alex

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: simsem and semTools support the blavaan object?
parts: I want to know simsem and semTools support the blavaan object.

I'm curious, what sort of support were you expecting from semTools?  Many of the semTools functions are redundant or useless in a Bayesian context (e.g., handling missing data, resampling methods for empirical CIs, using product-indicators for latent interactions, other data-preparation functions or functions that operate on input besides lavaan objects).  The reliability functions already works on blavaan objects because they are just based on point estimates, and the wald() function already works on blavaan objects because they have a vcov() method as well.  If you are looking for fit measures, you can already use the fitMeasures() function on blavaan objects to get the log-likelihood, PPP, and information criteria from the loo package.  If you want other fit measures to be available, you can request them on the blavaan group (Ed might already be planning to include them in a later version, perhaps even with credible intervals not available in a frequentist framework, except for RMSEA).  

The only semTools functions I can see a possible "need" for would be the measurement-invariance testing functions.  But if you are only fitting standard CFA models, I don't see the advantage of using a Bayesian estimator anyway.  BSEM would allow nice tricks like defining approximate measurement invariance via difference parameters that can be constrained to near-equality, but that is something the user would need to specify by changing the JAGS syntax that blavaan outputs.

If you have any specific requests, I suggest asking for them on the blavaan Google group.  The developers of lavaan, blavaan, and semTools can coordinate whether implementing functionality in semTools or the blavaan package itself would be best in the long run.
